subject: Intermittent livechat flow delay — customer advisory and short-term mitigations
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Summers <alex@fintools.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Jun 2024 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent livechat flow delay — customer advisory and short-term mitigations

Hi Alex —

We observed an increase in tail-latency affecting the streaming/chat endpoint for Fintools between approximately 08:50 and 09:05 UTC this morning. Symptoms: delayed token emission in streams (chunks arriving in 200–800ms bursts rather than steady pacing) and occasional 504s for long-running sessions. Impact appears limited to ~3% of active sessions in us-west region; we do not see data loss.

What we’ve done so far:
- Identified a transient edge-queue backlog concurrent with an autoscaler delay on a small set of serving hosts.
- Scoped affected customers via shard mapping; Fintools traffic was routed through the impacted edge pool between 08:52–09:01 UTC.

Immediate short-term mitigations we recommend and can apply on your behalf (quick rollbackable):
1) Switch to non-streaming fallback for affected routes (response_mode: "non-stream"): this returns the full response once generated and eliminates token-chunk pacing issues.
2) Reduce max_tokens and chunk_size on streaming calls (example: max_tokens: 400 -> 200, chunk_size: 32 -> 16).
3) Enable client-side pacing/retry: add exponential backoff for stream reconnects (recommended initial delay 200ms, cap 2s).

If you want us to apply #1 immediately we can toggle a per-route flag and route you to an unaffected host pool; this is fully reversible. That change typically takes 2–3 minutes to propagate.

Temporary workaround (curl example):
curl -sS https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/chat 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-chat-7b","input":"...","response_mode":"non-stream","max_tokens":200}'

We’ve attached a screenshot of the token pacing graph and a short console excerpt showing the error windows. We’ll open a formal incident ticket and follow up with a postmortem and a timeline.

Next steps for us:
- Confirm mitigation you prefer and proceed (we can apply #1 now).
- Post-incident: full RCA, corrective actions (autoscaler tuning + edge queue headroom), and any credits if SLA thresholds are breached.

I’m standing by to flip the non-stream flag if you want immediate relief.

Sorry for the disruption — we know streaming responsiveness is core to your UX.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: incident_screenshot_120624.png (PNG, token-emit timeline), console_log_excerpt_120624.txt (TXT, trimmed)

From: Alex Summers <alex@fintools.io>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Fintools Ops <ops@fintools.io>
Date: Wed, 12 Jun 2024 10:02:30 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent livechat flow delay — customer advisory and short-term mitigations

Thanks Hannah —

Appreciate the quick note. We saw the same behavior on our side (UX showed long stalls between tokens). Quick questions: if we switch to non-stream will that change latency for short responses? Will you apply that on our route now or do we need to change client code?

Also could you confirm whether this incident will be eligible for a credit under our SLA? Ops wants to understand the expected rollout time for the fix.

If you can apply the non-stream toggle now that’d be great; we can monitor and revert once things are stable.

—Alex
Head of Product
Fintools

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Summers <alex@fintools.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Jun 2024 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent livechat flow delay — customer advisory and short-term mitigations

On Wed, Jun 12, 2024 at 10:02 AM Alex Summers <alex@fintools.io> wrote:
> Thanks Hannah —
>
> Appreciate the quick note. We saw the same behavior on our side (UX showed long stalls between tokens). Quick questions: if we switch to non-stream will that change latency for short responses? Will you apply that on our route now or do we need to change client code?

Hi Alex —
Short answers:
- For short responses (<= ~150 tokens) non-stream latency will typically be similar or slightly better because the system avoids chunking overhead; for long responses it will increase tail latency but will eliminate intermittent chunking spikes.
- We can apply the per-route non-stream toggle immediately on our side; no client changes required.

I’ve applied the toggle for routes: projects/fintools/* at 11:08 PDT (propagated to US edge pool). Please monitor and let us know if you see improvement; we’ll keep it enabled while we confirm autoscaler and edge fixes.

Technical snippet we applied (internal):
route config: {
  "match": "projects/fintools/*",
  "overrides": { "response_mode": "non-stream", "max_tokens": 200 }
}

What we’ll do next:
- Ops will run an autoscaler tuning job today to reduce scale-up delay and increase burst headroom.
- We’ll re-run load tests against the impacted edge pool and adjust pre-warming.
- Postmortem and timeline: will aim to publish by EOD tomorrow with RCA and corrective actions.

SLA credits: we’ve logged INC-2024-06-1219; if the outage crosses the SLA threshold we will initiate a credit review as part of the postmortem delivery. I’ve added Ben to help coordinate credits and any contract-level questions.

Ben/Laura — I’ve applied the toggle and will monitor. Ben, please capture the exact host pool ids and the scaling metrics for the window 08:40–09:20 UTC and drop into the incident doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3ExampleIncidentDoc

Alex — thanks again for the quick signal. We’ll keep updates coming and confirm when we roll the streaming behavior back.

—Hannah

Fwding thread to close the loop internally. Summary of actions:
- Applied per-route non-stream override for projects/fintools/* at 11:08 PDT (see thread above).
- Monitoring shows token-chunk pacing normalized for Fintools sessions routed to new pool as of 11:20 PDT.
- Assigned follow-ups: Ben to gather autoscaler metrics and host pool ids (INC-2024-06-1219). Laura to draft postmortem outline and timeline (publish by 2024-06-13 EOD).
- Customer wants credit confirmation included in postmortem; we’ll surface SLA evaluation once RCA is complete.

I’ve attached the same artifacts we sent to the customer and the internal incident link. Please add anything missing to the doc before EOD.

Thanks,
Hannah
Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
